a short reflection on today’s gospel matthew 21:15-21 in today’s gospel jesus tells us to “repay to caesar what belongs to caesar and to god what belongs to god.” his words invite us to reflect on our priorities, our responsibilities and the place god holds in our lives. while we have duties to our families, communities and society, our relationship with god must always remain at the centre. giving to god what belongs to god means more than attending mass or saying our prayers. it means living our faith through love, kindness, forgiveness and compassion. when we care for the vulnerable, support those in need and reach out to the lonely, we make god's love visible through our actions. in the busyness of everyday life, we can sometimes forget to make time for god. today's gospel reminds us that our possessions and achievements should never take his place in our hearts. what matters most is how we use our gifts and blessings to serve god and others. as we reflect on today's gospel, let us ask ourselves: am i putting god first? am i using my gifts for the good of others? do my words and actions reflect the love of christ? may we have the courage to put god first, the generosity to serve others and the humility to recognise his presence in everyone we meet. lord, help us to give you what truly belongs to you: our hearts, our lives and our love. guide us to serve others with kindness and generosity, and may everything we say and do bring glory to your holy name. amen. prayer for vocations to the priesthood : st paul could have written this passage from today's second not only as words, but as power and the holy spirit and as utter conviction." mission sunday 2026 – one in christ, united in mission. mission sunday, celebrated today, sunday 18th october 2026, love god and your neighbour matthew 22:34–40 jesus brings us to the heart of faith: love god with our whole being and love our neighbour as ourselves. these commandments belong together. our prayer should shape how we treat others, especially those who inconvenience us, misunderstand us or cannot repay our kindness. to love god wholeheartedly is to bring him our fears, disappointments and weaknesses, trusting that we are loved even in our poverty. loving our neighbour means seeking their good through patience, forgiveness and honesty. and “as yourself” reminds us that we too are people god loves. humility acknowledges our faults while allowing us to receive his mercy. this gospel invites us to ask: are our prayers, plans and activities helping us become more loving? lord, let me receive your love today, and let that love shape how i treat the next person i meet. holy family parish draw our parish draw will begin in january 2027 to provide funds for the refurbishment and diocesan appointments - this weekend is fr lagan’s last weekend in our parish as our priest, i take the opportunity to thank him sincerely for his work both in the parish and the hospitals over the past four years. his endearing personality enabled him to get to know many people in a short period of time. his good humour and generosity of time have brought many blessings to many people and our parish community. as he begins a new phase of his life as parish priest in the sperrin parishes of gortin and greencastle, i on behalf of the parish, wish him every blessing. it will be a very big change for him so let’s keep him and all the priests involved in the latest diocesan appointments in our prayers. words of thanks from fr lagan on 18th august 2022, bishop donal mckeown appointed me to the parishes of glendermott and strathfoyle. on that occasion, even though it was a change, i very much knew that i was coming home. i was sent to a parish that i had previously served and for a short while after my ordination in 2012 began ministering as a priest. it is a place that i love very much and this last four years have been both a time of immense blessing. on 9th october, bishop router appointed me to the parishes of greencastle and gortin in co tyrone. whilst i am deeply honoured for his trust in me, i leave here with the best preparation i could ask for in taking up this new challenge. i want to thank all the staff of our parish, those who work to support the running of glendermott and strathfoyle, but especially to fr joshi for his kindness, guidance, support and friendship and to fr michael canny for his ever willing example, paternal guidance and endless patience not only during my time here but throughout my priestly ministry and also to each of you, for your prayers, your faith filled example and for the love and kindness that you have shown me, i will forever treasure. please keep me in your prayers and be assured of my prayers for you, your loved a common assumption is that love must just come, that it grows organically, and that it cannot be forced. that’s infatuation, not true love. any kind of love – for a parent, spouse, child, or friend – will reach a point during which it is no longer easy. for love to be true, it must be a free choice and commitment. ‘all your heart, soul, and mind’ sounds rather extreme, even rather dangerous. the world says that loving anyone totally is a risky proposition – what i f the one we love rejects us or lets us down, leaving us with nothing? and the world is even more terrified to love god totally, who cannot even be seen. this makes sense; after all, to love totally is to trust that we will find fulfillment precisely by not looking for it ourselves, but by looking to fulfill someone else. that old, almost clichéd phrase, ‘love grows when i t is given away,’ is actually spot-on in this regard. true love takes a leap of faith, which is what frightens nonbelievers. many people are okay with going to church every now and then or volunteering a charity from time to time (and posting it on instagram, of course). loving like that does not require us to make any kind of leap, any kind of definitive change, any commitment. but loving god with everything means that all we do is for love of him. we trust that he will take care of us. that is heroic; that is what it means to be a saint thought for the day ‘remember that nothing is small in the eyes of god. do all that you do with love.’ saint thérèse of lisieux ‘we have been called to heal wounds, to unite what fallen apart, and to bring home those who have lost their way.’ saint francis of assisi ‘i invite all christians, everywhere, at this very moment, to a renewed personal encounter with jesus christ, or at least an openness to letting him encounte r them; i ask all of you to do this unfailingly each da pope francis (eg 3) chiropodist clinic patricia barne will a end st columbcille centre, clonmany on wed oct 28 from 9am- 2pm. for an appointment call

calendar for the week ahead sunday 25th the greatest and first commandment; you must love you the lord our god with all your heart, soul and mind. the second resembles it: you must love your neighbour as yourself. tuesday 27th st otteran, is usually identified with odhran who preceded columba to iona. his death is recorded in 548 and his grave was greatly revered in iona. he was chosen by the vikings as patron of waterford in 1096 and later patron of the diocese. wednesday 28th st simon and st jude, apostles. nothing is known of simon except that he was born in cana and was called the zealot. jude, also known as thaddeus, was the apostle who a sked the lord at the last supper why he showed himself only to his disciples and not to the world. thursday 29th st colman , bishop. from kilmacduagh, co clare. founded two churches in aran, on inis mhór, before returning to kilmacduagh to make a further foundation there. saturday 31st blessed dominic collins (1566-1602) was born in youghal, co. cork. after a military career he joined the jesuits as a brother. he was captured in 1602 by the english who tried to make him abjure his faith. he was martyred in youghal on 31 october 1602. sunday 1st november all saints we celebrate the great company of all those who have gone before us and now enjoy the beatific vision, sharing in god’s life in the glory of heaven. 11.30am mass will be celebrated in ballybrack. reader at this mass will be miriam turnball mass this week in st pius x: monday to friday 10am. saturday 6.30pm; sunday 10am. confessions in st. pius x church : saturday 5.45pm to 6.15pm. the rosary and the divine mercy chaplet will be recited in st. pius x church, moville, at 7.30pm every day, from sunday – friday. adoration of the blessed sacrament on monday, 2-9pm; wednesday, 6-9pm. we offer our sympathy to the families and friends of robert carey, carrowbeg, who died recently. may they
